solves.reason: recall fits 'be able to ___ that event better'; various fits diverse odd actions listed; memorable fits positive conclusion about speech info.
watch fits 'adults ___ videos'; immediately fits 'tested memories ___ after descriptions and three weeks later' (two time points); spontaneously fits 'gestured on their own' with no instructions.

performing fits actions being carried out (chicken sliding, jogger bending); instructions fits 'gave adults no ___ about gesture' contrasted with earlier instructed group; encoded fits positive 'makes information memorable'.
'forget' contradicts the passage's whole point that gesture helps you recall/remember events; should be 'recall'.
'ordinary' contradicts 'various, sometimes odd, actions' — chicken sliding to a policeman etc. are odd/unusual, not ordinary.
'erased' contradicts 'makes the information ... memorable' — should be 'encoded', erased would mean forgotten not memorable.
blank replaces 'recall' — 'be able to recall that event better than if you don't gesture'.
blank replaces 'effects' — 'see if we'd get the same effects if people gestured on their own'.
blank replaces 'patterns' — 'We found the same patterns: people remembered items...'.
various = diverse (different kinds); others (similar, rare, narrow) don't match meaning.
immediately = instantly (right away).
odd = strange (unusual actions like chicken sliding to a policeman).
memorable (able to be remembered) is opposite of forgettable.
spontaneously (without being told/naturally) is opposite of deliberately (intentionally, on purpose).
(A) 'gate closed on its own' = by itself/스스로(힘으로); (B) 'own a house' = possess/소유하다.
'a movement of your hand, arm, or head that expresses what you think or feel' is the definition of gesture.
'a jogger bending down to touch his toes' — present participle modifying 'jogger', parallel structure with 'sliding' and 'swinging' in the list of actions.
Subject 'Producing gesture along with speech' is a singular gerund phrase, so the verb takes third-person singular form 'makes'.
'we gave the adults no instructions about gesture' — matches option 'no instructions', contrasting with the first experiment where they were told to gesture.
'tested the adults' memories of these events immediately after the descriptions and three weeks later' — matches 'immediately after the descriptions'.
